sources.title: Registered Backend Engineering manifest
claims: Domain engineering.backend is Backend Engineering, version 0.1.0, draft, owned by Albert, compatible with Kernel protocol 4.0.

Registered scope covers APIs, business logic, persistence, asynchronous processing, security, observability, reliability, and evidence-backed delivery; applicability and activation evidence are initially empty.

sources.title: Backend Engineering registry entry
claims: engineering.backend maps to domains/engineering/backend with version 0.1.0, draft status, and owner Albert.

sources.title: OpenAPI Specification v3.2.1, published 10 September 2026
claims: OpenAPI defines a programming-language-agnostic description of HTTP APIs.
Its objects describe paths, operations, parameters, request bodies, responses, schemas, and security requirements; it does not prescribe a server implementation language.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: Transaction Isolation
claims: Isolation levels have different concurrency guarantees; PostgreSQL Read Committed can observe different committed snapshots across successive statements.
Serializable execution may require retrying the complete transaction after a serialization failure; database-specific behavior must be checked.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: Modifying Tables
claims: Schema modification differs from data modification; table alterations include columns, constraints, defaults, and types.
Dropping a column removes its data; volatile defaults can require row updates, and constraints must be compatible with existing values.

sources.title: RabbitMQ: Consumer Acknowledgements and Publisher Confirms
claims: Publisher confirms and consumer acknowledgements cover distinct stages; a publisher confirmation does not prove business processing succeeded.
Acknowledgement modes affect data safety and memory pressure; negative acknowledgements can requeue, discard, or dead-letter deliveries according to configuration.

sources.title: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter, published 5 December 2019
sources.publisher: Amazon Web Services / Amazon Builders' Library
claims: Timeouts bound waiting and resource retention; retries can amplify overload, and timeout does not prove an operation had no side effects.
Idempotency, backoff, and jitter help make retries safer; timeout values require dependency-specific evidence.

sources.title: OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet
claims: REST services require protected transport, endpoint access control, input and content-type validation, and restrained error disclosure.
Server-side workflow state validation prevents bypass through out-of-order calls; authentication alone is insufficient.
Security audit logging and management-endpoint restrictions are part of API protection.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Concepts: Signals, modified 10 March 2026
claims: Telemetry signals describe runtime system activity; OpenTelemetry collects, processes, and exports signals.
Traces describe request paths, metrics capture measurements, and logs record events; these signals provide complementary observations.

sources.title: Site Reliability Engineering, Chapter 17: Testing for Reliability
claims: Unit, integration, system, regression, and performance tests provide different evidence at different costs.
Hermetic test results and live production behavior differ; configuration and rollout combinations can invalidate operational assumptions.

sources.title: The Site Reliability Workbook, Chapter 16: Canarying Releases
claims: Release engineering benefits from reproducible builds, automated tests and deployments, and small changes.
A canary is a partial, time-limited deployment evaluated against a control before deciding whether to continue rollout.

capability_hypotheses.description: Define and revise service contracts, request/response validation, errors, security requirements, and compatibility evidence using the repository's chosen protocol and schema tooling.
Implement explicit server-side business invariants and workflow transitions, including rejection of unauthorized, invalid, and out-of-order operations.
Design bounded persistence operations and transaction boundaries; verify isolation, concurrency anomalies, and complete-transaction retry behavior against the selected database.
Plan and validate schema/data changes with existing-data checks, compatibility sequencing, destructive-change disclosure, and a recovery or forward-repair path.
Specify asynchronous acceptance versus processing completion, acknowledgement timing, duplicate handling, failure disposition, and bounded worker concurrency.
Bound dependency waits and retry attempts; justify timeout budgets, idempotency, backoff, and jitter using the selected client and service behavior.
Apply transport, authentication integration, authorization, request validation, safe errors, audit logging, and management-surface restrictions with negative test evidence.
Instrument service requests and asynchronous work with appropriate traces, metrics, and logs, and verify that emitted signals can support diagnosis.

Produce reproducible, risk-appropriate unit, integration, system, concurrency, failure, and performance evidence; distinguish local tests from deployed acceptance and define monitored rollout/recovery criteria.

Keep the reusable Domain independent of one language, framework, database, broker, or cloud; select concrete tools from downstream repository evidence and verify their official contracts before implementation.

organizational_gaps.description: Project reviewers, service owners, security approvers, and independent acceptance authorities are unknown and must be resolved for downstream work.
Repository, database, infrastructure, production-access, data-mutation, deployment, and publication permissions are unknown; no such permission is inferred from Domain activation.
Internal architecture, API compatibility rules, security baseline, data classification, retention, audit, and regulatory obligations are unknown.
Product language/runtime/framework versions, database/broker semantics, topology, existing service boundaries, and private architecture are unknown.
Actual product build, lint, test, migration, integration-environment, rollout, and rollback commands and credentials are unknown; do not invent executable commands.
Project traffic, latency/availability objectives, capacity limits, retry budgets, alert thresholds, recovery objectives, and on-call arrangements are unknown.
Task-specific approvals, approved scope, deployment authority, release evidence, and production acceptance are unknown; public-source research is not approval or acceptance evidence.
